question:
**Fill in the blanks: **

The Sarkaria Commission (Centre-State Relations) was set up in the year ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1983**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sarkaria Commission was established by the Government of India in **1983** to examine and review the working of existing arrangements between the Central and State governments.
 
• The commission was chaired by Justice R.S. Sarkaria, a former judge of the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Its primary objective was to recommend changes to improve the relationship and distribution of powers between the Centre and States.
 
• The Sarkaria Commission submitted its report in **1988**, providing detailed recommendations on various issues concerning federal governance in India.
 
• The commission emphasized cooperative federalism and suggested ways to strengthen the autonomy of states while maintaining the unity of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: 1990**

 
 
• This year does not align with the establishment of the Sarkaria Commission.
 
• However, during the early 1990s, significant political changes occurred in India, including the rise of coalition governments which further highlighted the importance of Centre-State relations.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: 1992**
 
 
• 1992 marks the introduction of the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, which provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and urban local bodies.
 
• These amendments focused on decentralization and strengthening grassroots governance but are unrelated to the Sarkaria Commission.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: 2000**
 
 
• In 2000, India witnessed administrative reforms such as the formation of new states like Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Uttarakhand.
 
• While these changes impacted Centre-State relations, they are not connected to the establishment of the Sarkaria Commission.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Centre-State Relations in India**
 
 
• India has a quasi-federal structure, where powers are distributed between the Centre and States as per the Constitution.
 
• The Sarkaria Commission was a landmark initiative to address challenges in this arrangement and recommend measures for effective governance.
 
• Key recommendations included guidelines for the imposition of President’s Rule, principles for the appointment of Governors, and the role of the Inter-State Council.
 
• Many of its recommendations continue to influence debates and policies on federalism in India.
